n-ai-inference-markets.title: AI inference market coins
n-ai-inference-markets.summary: Coins on Pons (Robinhood Chain) whose own metadata describes selling or crediting AI model inference. Orbio.so (ORBIO): "Hold $ORBIO, earn OpenRouter credits. Half of trading fees are converted into inference credits and paid to holders, in dollars." Its site (orbio.so, e3:1) offers LLM credits at a discount, "one key, every model", and lists 468 models; its pool was created on 2026-09-20. useorbix.app (ORBIX): "AI inference marketplace bringing leading models into one platform." Its site (useorbix.app, e3:0) says sellers list spare capacity and the cheapest offer serves each request, that 1.2% of every ORBIX buy and sell on Pons pays into a daily subsidy pool, and that ORBIX holders get a discount; its pool was created at 05:24 UTC on 2026-10-23. Raeto (RAETO): "Your tokenized stocks pay for your AI inference. Lend on Morpho, earn credits for 400+ models." Posts from the project's account @RaetoCC on 2026-10-18 and 2026-10-19 (e3:3) describe rCREDIT, AI credits as a token said to be backed 1:1 by USDG, and a Borro integration; its pool was created on 2026-10-12. A competing marketplace, Surplus, posted on 2026-10-19 (e3:3) that it is in Raeto's chat and API. Every description is the projects' own claim: volumes, discounts, backing, fee routing and payouts are not verified here, and the three coins are separate products with no shown link to each other or to any lab.

n-php2shell.notice: Posts of 2026-10-23 and 2026-10-24 (e1:7, e1:8): Qualys (2026-10-23 19:47 UTC) calls PHP2Shell two critical PHP flaws (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, CVSS 9.2) and says attack traffic has been reported; @IntCyberDigest (2026-10-24 03:14 UTC) says PHP disclosed a further unpatched remote code execution flaw, CVE-2026-115560, two days after the emergency fixes, that needs an unusual setup, with no emergency release planned and a mitigation of session.upload_progress.enabled=0. Two posts from the same account disagree on whether exploitation in the wild is confirmed (e1:7).
n-php2shell.interpretation: The vulnerability story is real and still being covered by security vendors, but the coins are copies launched around it and nothing links them to the PHP project, the researchers or Sury. The newest post concerns a different CVE that the four coins' metadata does not mention. Four coins trade $745K across the discovery sweep; most of the volume is PHP-UP-2026 and the two PHP2SHELL coins trade far above their market caps (see the volume caveat).
